steps: This video shows why a prompt needs four elements, role, context, task and format, to get a consistent answer. Maya uploads a twenty page client contract and types just two words: summarize this.
Claude has to fill the blanks itself. Who is this for, and why? It guesses, and sends back a three sentence overview.
Maya sends the same file and the same prompt again. Run two returns a two page bullet list, and run three a table. The output drifts, because nothing in the prompt pins it down.
Her manager spots the gap. Maya said what she wanted, but not who it is for, why she needs it, or what format to use. A good prompt covers role, context, task and format.
So Maya rewrites the prompt: you are a contract analyst, the audience is the C F O, keep it to one page, in three bullet sections.
Claude returns a one page summary with three sections: payment, renewal and liability. With nothing left to guess, reruns converge on the same consistent answer.

Finally, Maya sends the one page summary to the C F O, who reads it before the board meeting. Spell out role, context, task and format, and Claude stops guessing. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
